questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was able to study Indigenous Studies and Inuktitut language at the University of Toronto, I wanted to continue my linguistic language courses, since I have Inuit-language courses in Inuttut (kalaallisut/westgreenlandic) at the University of Toronto

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Language courses in Inuktitut were cancelled and I wasn't able to take courses in Inuktitut, though I took courses in Indigenous Studies and related to and was happy that I was able to!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was ok easy, but it was so difficult to find a place to stay. Information about rentals, housing was very difficult to understand.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got no assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: International students didn't get to know eachother much, we didn't get to mingle, barely introduced. So it was difficult to really find a community.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was hard, I found mine last minute, but it was not great. It turned out to be really bad and had black mold in it affecting my health/mental health including my motivation to study as I got headaches and caughs all the time when home

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I had someone look for the place to rent, but it wasn't enogh to secure a great place. 

Rather rent a sublet and don't take over, then you'll be able to get out of the apartement and move somewhere else as it will not be your responsibility if you don't take over.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Courses in Inuktitut cancelled made me sad, I would have wanted to be able to switch to another institution in Canada since my desired courses were cancelled.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was too much administrative work. I don't know how to describe it since there was soo much to go through.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I really liked the course calendar that gave you an idea how your courses would be scheduled in order to take courses that didn't overlap.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, but there was a course that I really wanted to take where I got rejected but in my opinion could have taken: Toxic Worlds, Decolonial Futures

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose courses that you desire to take, check who lectures and choose wisely

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I originally had 4 courses and was happy to go down to 3. 

In two of the courses there was very high acedemic descussions, but in the two others people didn't speak to eachother so it was very awkward. Even though the academic material and lectures were great.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very hard to compare, but I feel that classes at UCPH are more lively and are open to student that haven't read for class and are able to structure class so that everyone understands and are able to gain as much as those who have read for class, more friendly.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- ANT366H1: Anthropology of Activism and Social Justice
- INS390H1: Research and Ethics in Indigenous Studies
- WGS390H1: Land-ing: Indigenous and Black Futurist Spaces
- CRI364H1: Indigenous Peoples & Criminal Justice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Anthropology of Activism and Social Justice; Land-ing: Indigenous and Black Futurist Spaces; Research and Ethics in Indigenous Studies

Because of the knowledge gained but also for the amazing professors at the courses

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was much cheaper than expected, travel by plane to other parts in Canada expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a great museum, gym and a variety of places to buy your meal at campus

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visiting the museums and go to the parks and outer areas of town.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going to Ottawa, Montreal and other places in Canada is highly recommended

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult as it was also very difficult to find new friends and a community, but the First Nations House gave me an opportunity to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I really enjoyed being at the First Nations House, they made me feel home and that I belong, so I built a community there. It was a great place to be as an Indigenous Student, as an Inuk from Inuit Nunaat (Greenland)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The students didn't speak at lectures and not even between each other, something that lectors and professors also kept mentioning if it was only a Toronto phenomenon.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The big city mentality, everything busy all the time, no one having time for each other. Difficult to plan and meet since people live far from each other.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find a place to stay at campus or rent something in the outer suburbs of town.
Engage with fellow exchange students.
Engage with the Indigenous People and learn from them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find events that interrests you at Folio which is the place where you find most of the events at the U of T, also be up to date on the U of T website as there can be other relevent event there that are not on Folio.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting fellow Indigenous Students and people from all around the world and to be able to talk about our studies with especially fellow Indigenous Students and professors/lectors

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Housing as it had bad implications on my studies and my health affecting my mental health as well, I was diagnosed with stress after coming home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
